ayahs.1: We have granted you, O Prophet, a clear triumph—victory that looked like setback but opened the path to far greater openings.
ayahs.2: So that Allah may forgive you what came before and what follows, complete His favour upon you, and guide you on the Straight Path.
ayahs.3: And so that Allah may support you with mighty support.
ayahs.4: He is the One who sent tranquillity into the hearts of the mu'min so their iman would grow. To Allah belong the forces of the heavens and the earth. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
ayahs.5: So He may admit believing men and women into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to remain forever, and absolve their sins. That is the supreme success with Allah.
ayahs.6: And so He may punish hypocrite men and women and those who commit shirk—giving devotion owed to Allah alone to other powers—men and women who think evil thoughts about Allah. Ill fate is theirs. Allah is displeased with them, has condemned them, and prepared Hell for them—an evil destination.
ayahs.7: To Allah belong the forces of the heavens and the earth. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
ayahs.8: We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad news, and a warner,
ayahs.9: so that people may have iman in Allah and His Messenger, honour and support him, and glorify Allah morning and evening.
ayahs.10: Those who pledge allegiance to you are in truth pledging allegiance to Allah. His Hand is over theirs. Whoever breaks that pledge harms only himself. Whoever fulfils what he pledged to Allah will receive a great reward.
ayahs.11: The desert Arabs who stayed behind will say: We were held back by our wealth and families—ask forgiveness for us. They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say: Who can protect you from Allah if He intends harm or benefit for you? Allah is fully aware of what you do.
ayahs.12: The truth is you thought the Messenger and the mu'min would never return to their families. That thought was made to look attractive in your hearts, you harboured evil assumptions about Allah, and you became a doomed people.
ayahs.13: Whoever does not have iman in Allah and His Messenger—We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who reject the truth.
ayahs.14: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. Allah is All-Forgiving, the Rahim.
ayahs.15: Those who stayed behind will say, when you set out for spoils of war: Let us come with you. They wish to change Allah's promise. Say: You will not come with us. Allah has already said so. They will say: You are jealous of us. In truth, they barely understand.
ayahs.16: Say to the desert Arabs who stayed behind: You will be called to fight a people of great might. You will fight them unless they submit. If you obey, Allah will give you a fine reward. If you turn away as you did before, He will inflict a painful punishment on you.
ayahs.17: No blame rests on the blind, the lame, or the sick for staying behind. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted into Gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whoever turns away will suffer a painful punishment.
ayahs.18: Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, sent tranquillity down upon them, and rewarded them with a victory close at hand
ayahs.19: and abundant spoils they would take. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
ayahs.20: Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will take. He has hastened this for you and held people's hands back from harming you—so it may be a sign for the mu'min and so He may guide you on the Straight Path.
ayahs.21: And there are other victories not yet within your reach that Allah has already encompassed. Allah is capable of everything.
ayahs.22: If those who reject the truth were to fight you, they would turn and flee. They would find no protector and no helper.
ayahs.23: This is Allah's established way with those who passed before. You will find no change in Allah's way.
ayahs.24: He is the One who held their hands back from you and your hands back from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you the upper hand over them. Allah sees everything you do.
ayahs.25: They are the ones who persisted in denial and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, keeping the sacrificial animals from reaching their place. Had there not been believing men and women among them whom you did not know—whom you might have trampled unknowingly, incurring guilt—Allah would have let you march through. He admits into His mercy whomever He wills. Had those hidden believers been separate, We would have punished those who rejected the truth with a painful punishment.
ayahs.26: When those who rejected the truth filled their hearts with the arrogance of pre-Islamic ignorance, Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and the believers, and bound them to the declaration of tawhid—they were more entitled to it and worthier of it. Allah has perfect knowledge of everything.
ayahs.27: Allah will fulfil His Messenger's true vision: you will enter the Sacred Mosque, in sha' Allah, in security—some with heads shaved and some with hair shortened—without fear. He knew what you did not know, and granted you first the triumph already at hand.
ayahs.28: He is the One who sent His Messenger with right guidance and the deen of truth, so it may prevail over every other way. Allah is sufficient as Witness.
ayahs.29: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Those with him are firm against those who reject the truth and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating in salah, seeking Allah's bounty and pleasure. The mark of their prostration shows on their faces. This is their description in the Torah. Their parable in the Gospel is a seed that sends out its shoot, then strengthens it, then grows thick and stands firm on its stem, delighting the sower—so Allah makes the believers a source of dismay to those who deny. To those among them who have iman and do good, Allah has promised forgiveness and a great reward.
